# Organization Tree Reference

Complete reference for the `glassfrog tree` and `glassfrog subroles` commands — the circle-hierarchy reads that expose the nesting between roles.

## Overview

Two sibling top-level commands expose the role hierarchy:

- `glassfrog tree [ROLE_ID]` — reads the whole organization tree (no positional) or the subtree rooted at a role (one positional), as a single nested document. Neither is paginated; `--depth` bounds size.
- `glassfrog subroles <ROLE_ID>` — lists a role's immediate child roles (one level). This read is paginated.

These are distinct from `glassfrog roles` (the org-wide list + single read) and from the token-scoped `glassfrog me roles`.

Codebase enrichment skipped — not attempted. This reference is based on the interface contracts only.

## `glassfrog tree` — org tree and rooted subtree

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog tree [ROLE_ID] [--depth N] [--include a,b,…] [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ROLE_ID` | string | optional | Omitted → whole-org tree (anchor role as root). Present → subtree rooted at that role (`role_…`). Not validated locally; the API resolves it (unknown/malformed → `404`). |

More than one positional is rejected as a usage error with no API call. Each tree read issues exactly one request and renders the full nested document, bounded by `--depth` when given. There is no walk, no first-page opt-out, and no incompleteness note.

### Tree flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--depth` | int (optional) | omitted = full subtree | Maximum descendant depth (`depth` query). `0` → root node alone; `1` → root plus direct children; and so on. Sent only when present, so `--depth 0` is distinct from omitting it. A negative value is a fail-fast usage error before any request. |
| `--include` | string (comma-separated) | — | Per-node related resources to embed (`?include=`). Validated locally before any request; an unsupported value is a fail-fast usage error. |

> `--first-page` and `--per-page` are **rejected on `tree`** — the tree reads are unpaginated.

### `--include` targets (tree)

| Value | Embedded per node |
|---|---|
| `accountabilities` | The node's accountabilities. |
| `domains` | The node's domains. |
| `members` | The node's members (actors). |

### Tree output

**`full`** — a depth-indented tree (two spaces per level), one node per block, root flush-left:

```
<Role Name> (role_0123…) [structural,elected]
  Purpose: <purpose | (no purpose set)>
  <Child Name> (role_0456…)
    Purpose: <purpose | (no purpose set)>
    <Grandchild Name> (role_0789…)
      Purpose: …
```

When `--include` is set, each node also renders one guarded section per requested resource, indented under that node (omitted when not requested; explicit-absence marker when requested but empty):

```
  Accountabilities:
    - <accountability description> | (none)
  Domains:
    - <domain description> | (none)
  Members:
    - <actor name> (per_… | agt_…) | (none)
```

**Depth-boundary signal** — a node whose API `has_subroles` is `true` but whose children are not in the result (because `--depth` capped beneath it, or the API withheld them) is rendered with an explicit marker so it is not mistaken for a true leaf:

```
  <Branch Name> (role_0456…)  (+ subroles below depth)
```

A node with no children **and** `has_subroles: false` is a true leaf — rendered with nothing indented and no marker. The marker is driven solely by the API's `has_subroles` boolean; it never invents a count of omitted descendants.

**`compact`** — one line per node, depth shown by leading indentation, id first then double-space-separated fragments. `has_subroles` is rendered so a depth-capped node is distinct from a true leaf:

```
role_0123…  <Role Name>  children=<N>  has_subroles=<yes|no>  flags=<structural,elected | —>
  role_0456…  <Child Name>  children=<N>  has_subroles=<yes|no>  flags=<—>
```

**`json` / `yaml`** — the raw API payload verbatim.

**Empty result** — `tree` on a leaf root (or `--depth 0`): the root node renders alone with no children indented, exit `0`. If that root's `has_subroles` is `true` (a `--depth 0` cut over a non-empty circle), it carries the depth-boundary marker.

## `glassfrog subroles <ROLE_ID>` — immediate children

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog subroles <ROLE_ID> [--include a,b,…] [--first-page] [--per-page N] [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ROLE_ID` | string | **required** | The parent role whose direct children are listed (`role_…`). Not validated locally; the API resolves it (unknown → `404`). |

Missing or extra positionals are rejected as a usage error with no API call. Lists immediate child roles, one level only.

### Subroles flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--include` | string (comma-separated) | — | Per-child related resources to embed (`?include=`). Validated locally before any request; an unsupported value is a fail-fast usage error. |
| `--first-page` | bool | false | Fetch only the first page and signal if more exist (see [Subroles completeness signalling](#subroles-completeness-signalling)). |
| `--per-page` | int | API max | Page size for the walk. The API owns the valid range. |

> `--depth` is **rejected on `subroles`** — depth bounds a recursive tree; subroles returns one level.

### `--include` targets (subroles)

| Value | Embedded per child |
|---|---|
| `assignments` | The child's assignments. |
| `subroles` | The child's immediate sub-roles. |
| `parent_role` | The child's parent role. |
| `policies` | The child's policies. |
| `notes` | The child's notes. |
| `skills` | The child's skills (summaries). |

### Subroles output

**`full`** — one block per child role (the role-block shape), blocks separated by a blank line; with `--include`, one guarded section per requested resource per child.

**`compact`** — one line per child:

```
role_0456…  <Child Name>  has_subroles=<yes|no>
```

**`json` / `yaml`** — `subroles` is a walked list read: it aggregates every page into a single synthesized `{"data":[…]}` document and **drops per-page `meta`**, so the shape stays stable across the walk (and under `--first-page`). Each child's bytes are preserved verbatim inside `data`; only the top-level envelope is synthesized. Completeness is signalled on stderr, not via in-band `meta`. (Contrast `tree`, a single read that emits the raw nested document verbatim.) See [Structured Serialization](structured-serialization.md).

**Empty result** — `subroles` on a leaf role: under `full`/`compact`, stdout is exactly `No subroles.` and the command exits `0`. Under `json`/`yaml`, stdout is the empty aggregate `{"data":[]}`, not the API's original page envelope.

## Subroles completeness signalling

`subroles` is paginated. A partial list is never silently presented as complete. Completeness is signalled via a note on **stderr**.

| Situation | Behaviour | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| Default (full walk) | Walks every page and renders the complete child set. | 0 |
| `--first-page`, more pages exist | Renders the first page; writes to stderr: `note: more subroles exist than shown; re-run without --first-page to fetch all` | 0 |
| Mid-walk failure | Renders children gathered so far; writes to stderr: `note: result is incomplete — <cause>; the subroles shown are a partial set` | non-zero |

The tree reads carry no incompleteness note — the single response is the complete (depth-bounded) tree.

stdout carries only the rendered result (or `No subroles.`); all diagnostics and incompleteness notes go to stderr.

## Output formats

Inherited persistent root flags, read by cobra inheritance:

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--base-url URL` | Override the API base URL (top rung of the base-URL precedence chain). |
| `-o`, `--output FORMAT` | `full` (default), `compact`, `json`, or `yaml`. Resolution chain: flag → `GLASSFROG_OUTPUT` → `.glassfrogrc output` → `full`. |

The raw API envelope is never emitted under a human format (`full`/`compact`). The commands issue a plain `GET` and send no `If-None-Match` (no conditional-request caching).

## Exit codes and errors

Errors go to **stderr**; the exit code is the category from the Exit-Code Convention. Every message names the cause and a next step, and never includes the token.

| Condition | Exit | stderr message |
|---|---|---|
| Tree read / subroles listed (incl. leaf root, empty subroles) | 0 | — (result on stdout; subroles incompleteness note on stderr when applicable) |
| No usable token | 2 | "not authenticated — run `glassfrog auth login`" |
| Unreadable / malformed credential file | 1 | names the path — "fix or remove the malformed `.glassfrogrc`" |
| Unknown/forbidden role id, bad `depth` (API `400`), or other non-2xx | 3 / 4 / 5 | names the HTTP status + extracted detail; per-class next step |
| Could not reach the wire | 6 | names the transport failure + host — "check network access and the base URL" |
| 2xx body did not match the expected shape | 1 | "the API response did not match the expected shape — may be an API change; report it" |
| Malformed paging mid-walk (subroles) | 1 | "the API returned malformed pagination — partial set shown" |
| Base-URL configuration error | 2 | names the malformed base URL + source |
| Invalid `--output` selector | 2 | names the bad format value + the four valid names |
| Unsupported `--include` value | 2 | names the unsupported value + the running read's supported set; no request sent |
| Negative `--depth` | 2 | "--depth must be 0 or greater"; no request sent |
| `--depth` on `subroles`, `--first-page`/`--per-page` on `tree`, missing/extra positional | 2 | names the misuse (e.g. "--depth applies to a tree read; subroles returns one level") |

Exit codes by category: `0` success, `1` runtime error, `2` usage error, `3` API error, `4` permission error, `5` rate-limited, `6` network unavailable.
